thread.title: Netflix to issue $1.5 billion of junk bonds to finance its massive spending plans

author: morningstar.com
title: Netflix to issue $1.5 billion of junk bonds to finance its massive spending plans
text:
By Ciara Linnane, MarketWatch
Streaming giant is planning to spend up to $8 billion on content this year
Netflix Inc. is once again tapping the corporate bond market with plans to issue $1.5 billion of high-yield, or "junk," bonds to help finance its huge spending plans for 2018.
The company said it will use proceeds of the deal for working capital, including content acquisition and production and even for potential acquisitions or other transactions. The company has said it will spend between $7.5 billion to $8.0 billion on content this year.
S&P Global Ratings said its B-plus corporate rating and positive outlook are not affected by the deal, as the company's adjusted leverage will remain at about 4.1 times.
"However, we expect adjusted leverage to increase slightly to the low- to mid-4x area as Netflix continues to borrow to invest heavily in content in 2018," S&P analyst Jawad Hussain wrote in a note.
S&P is expecting Netflix (NFLX) to remain the leading streaming video on demand service, even as competition heats up with Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) already active in the field and Apple Inc. (AAPL) expected to follow suit (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apples-1-billion-tv-move-pits-company-against-spotify-not-netflix-2017-08-21).
See now:Netflix sees sharks approaching from both sides in Apple and Disney (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/netflix-sees-sharks-approaching-from-both-sides-in-apple-and-disney-2018-01-22)
Hussain pointed to the company's success in raising prices last year while growing its subscriber base. The company is expected to continue to spend heavily on original content to retain and expand that base and make its offering more attractive to consumers.
"This supports its ability to add subscribers while raising prices over time," he wrote. "However, we expect the significant investment in content and marketing will result in free cash flow deficits in excess of $3 billion in 2018."
Netflix last week stunned investors with first-quarter earnings (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/netflix-earnings-live-blog-2018-04-16)that blew past earnings estimates. The company added 7.4 million more streaming subscribers, more than the 6.6 million expected, with 5 million of them outside the U.S.
See also: These are the DVDs that kept the post office busiest in each of Netflix's first 20 years (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/these-are-the-dvds-that-kept-the-post-office-busiest-in-each-of-netflixs-20-years-2018-04-09)
Related:Hollywood has never seen competition like Netflix (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/hollywood-has-never-seen-competition-like-netflix-2017-10-18)
Higher subscription prices for the service, combined with the growing customer base, gave a huge boost to revenue -- Netflix said its 43% year-over-year jump in streaming revenue was its best in history.
The company further surprised with net income of $290.1 million, more in three months than for all of 2016. If the company meets its second-quarter forecast of $358 million in profit, it will earn more in the first half of 2018 than all of 2017, when it reported an annual profit of $558.9 million.
For more, read: Netflix is growing at a stunning rate -- and so is its profit (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/netflix-is-growing-even-faster-and-streaming-to-record-profit-totals-2018-04-16)
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/netflix-is-growing-even-faster-and-streaming-to-record-profit-totals-2018-04-16)CreditSights analysts reiterated their market perform rating on Netflix bonds in the wake of the quarterly report and said while they are positive on the operating outlook for the company in 2018, "this view is balanced by the expectation for repeated issuance to fund negative cash flow."
Netflix had total debt outstanding of $6.5 billion at quarter end, up about $3.2 billion from the first quarter of 2017. Total cash on hand came to $2.6 billion at quarter end.
Netflix does not have pending debt maturities in the near term, they said. The next significant maturity is 2021, when $500 million of 5.375% notes mature.
The company's most active bonds, the 4.875% notes that mature in April of 2028, were last Quote: d at 96.50 cents on the dollar, to yield 5.332%, according to MarketAxess, or at a yield spread of 239 basis points over Treasurys.
See: These are the 2 things Netflix investors still need to worry about, analysts say (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/analysts-applaud-netflix-for-another-home-run-quarter-2018-04-17)
On the equity side, shares were up 0.4%, but have gained 71% in 2018 so far, while the S&P has gained 0.03% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average has fallen 1.1%.
Read now: Can Facebook, Apple and Google keep powering tech's growth? (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/can-facebook-apple-and-google-keep-powering-techs-growth-2018-04-21)
